title: Proposed NSW laws to allow coalmine to increase production pose ‘serious corruption risk’
summary_full: Bill to authorise expansion at Mount Pleasant coalmine, subject to a landmark high court decision, will be debated this weekGet our daily political email, free app or daily news podcastA New South Wales government bill to increase coal production at a Hunter Valley coalmine creates a “serious corruption risk” for the state due to a clause that would give the resources minister “king-like” powers, the barrister and anti-corruption campaigner Geoffrey Watson says.The state parliament will this week debate legislation to allow MACH Energy to increase coal production at the Mount Pleasant mine in Muswellbrook by 32% to 16.5m tonnes per year.
